A distinct benefit of DXA is its ability to estimate segmental lean mass for the arms, trunk, and legs. Validated equations have been developed to calculate skeletal muscle mass from DXA-derived data (49), although the algorithm was found to have an unexplained systematic bias that overestimates the variable in Caucasians (38). Nevertheless, DXA is often considered a surrogate measure for hypertrophy and was recently deemed the reference standard for measuring muscle mass by a European Society for Clinical and Economic Aspects of Osteoporosis and Osteoarthritis working group on frailty and sarcopenia (1 1).
